MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 15, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on September 15, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 10, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Schlicht

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

RECESS

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:04
p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Schlicht was absent.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

City Council Minutes  1  September 15, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Ziggy Wilczynski as a Hometown Hero

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Ziggy Wilczynski.

P2. Proclaim September 20, 2014, to be Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans Day

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to the Welcome Home Vietnam Event
  Chairperson, Barbara Liddy, and Vietnam Veterans and members of the Committee Pat
  Rizco, Jim Wallace, Sandy Hill, Dennis Lumley, Ed Fuller, Mike Waugh and Wes Bickel.

P3. Featured Business of the Month - Shanghai Place

  Mayor Kelley read the proclamation and thanked the owner of Shanghai Place, Helen Cheung
  (Helen was unable to attend the meeting).

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Carol Weidler, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for the moving 9/11 tribute last week. She
also thanked the City for supporting the Mission Viejo High School salute to veterans football
game and she noted that MVHS even won the game.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he objects to the award of a contract to Townsend Public
Affairs for the 7th year in a row. He feels that Townsend has a conflict of interest and while
reviewing background material on lobbyists, he learned that City Council candidate Wendy
Bucknum is a lobbyist herself. He stated that lobbying is a potential threat to political integrity
and should be shunned.

Gurpreet S. Ahuja, M.D.: speaking as a member of the Board of Directors of Orange County
Human Relations Commission, he shared information on some of the work that OCHR has been
involved in in the City of Mission Viejo and he distributed copies of the OCHR annual report. Mr.
Ahuja presented Mayor Kelley with a certificate of appreciation for the City's partnership on
human relations matters.

Margot Ferron, M.V.: announced that the September 5 Stand Up to Cancer event was wildly
successful and they raised $3,000. She thanked the City Council for always supporting cancer
awareness events and other worthy causes.

Consent Calendar as described below.

3.  Check Register Dated August 22, 2014 in the Amount of $2,991,336.41

City Council Minutes  3  September 15, 2014

7.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2013-14 and Annual Review of City’s

City Council Minutes  4  September 15, 2014

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Reardon

23. Ordinance Prohibiting Minors from Possessing E-Cigarette Devices

  Council Member Reardon presented her report.

  City Attorney Curley provided information on the implementation of the proposed ordinance.
  He stated that this ordinance would bring a minor’s possession of e-cigarettes into a parallel
  level of enforcement with possession of regular cigarettes.

  OCSD Lieutenant Brad NewMyer read a letter from Sheriff Hutchens expressing support for
  the proposed ordinance.

  Marilyn MacDougall, M.V.: stated that scientific studies are not complete and the
  repercussions of e-cigarette use are not known yet. She commended Council Member
  Reardon for bringing this to the Council's attention and she expressed her support for the
  ordinance.

  Linda Shephard, M.V.: stated that she had to take an e-cigarette device away from her honor-
  student son and she would support an ordinance that would make possession of the devices
  illegal for minors.

City Council Minutes  5  September 15, 2014
   Garett Matthews, M.V.: announced that as a student, he has witnessed a trend with minors
  using e-cigarettes. He noted that more kids are using e-cigs and schools and administrators
  are having zero tolerance with them.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance 14-XXX Establishing a Prohibition Upon a Minor Possessing, for Any Purpose,
  a Device That Vaporizes Any Substance for Use as a Recreational Inhalant, or for Non-
  Doctor Prescribed Medical or Psychological Purposes, or for Any Purpose Other Than as
  May Be Prescribed By a Licensed Medical Doctor.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Reardon
  NOES:  Leckness and Ury
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

OLD BUSINESS

15. Montanoso Locker Room Renovation (CIP 500)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1) award
  a contract to JR Universal Construction in an amount not to exceed $820,764.00 and (2)
  adopt Resolution 14-43 Amending the Budget for CIP 500 by $30,000.
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

16. Sierra Recreation Center Play Area (CIP 323)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award a contract to
  Hondo Company, Inc. for the construction of the north Sierra Recreation Center Play Area
  in an amount not to exceed $257,294.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

City Council Minutes  6  September 15, 2014
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the City Manager needs to correct his statements from
  the last meeting regarding Mission Viejo's liability for OCFA's unfunded actuarial accrued
  liabilities (UAAL.) He asked the Council to direct the City Attorney to provide a written
  opinion regarding his verbal assertion that the City is not liable for the UAAL and to provide
  a resume for the new City Attorney. Finally, Mr. Wontrobski asked Mayor Kelley to explain
  to the public the basis for the judge's ruling against OCFA on the validation agreement which,
  he said, the judge determined was a gift of public funds.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

20. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars

City Council Minutes  7  September 15, 2014
 Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon thanked everyone who participated in the Mission Viejo High School
football game for the armed forces. There were many more veterans participating this year and
the young people at MVHS are very respectful and supportive of the military. She stated that it is
such a wonderful experience to participate in that event. Council Member Reardon reminded
residents of the Vietnam Veterans recognition on Saturday, September 20, 2014, beginning at
11:00 a.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. She stated that the purpose of the event
is to really honor Vietnam vets who were treated so shamefully when many of them returned
home. Residents Dennis Lumley and Wes Bickel are going to be speaking and Wes, a decorated
Marine, will share a story that he never told until last year. Council Member Reardon noted that
many Vietnam vets have not talked about their experiences and much of that is because of how
they were received when they came home.

Council Member Schlicht

Mayor Kelley announced that Council Member Schlicht has 10 agenda items under her name
which are items that were removed from previous Consent Calendars. Council Member Ury noted
that the items date back to July.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve agenda
items 24 through 33.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that the 9/11 service was phenomenal. The attendees loved it and
Tom Frost, whose daughter Lisa was a passenger on one of the airplanes that crashed into the
World Trade Center, was a guest at the event. Mr. Frost told the story of how he wore Lisa’s
Boston Marathon jacket after she died. He also recounted his conversation with Lisa the very
morning that she passed away. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that not every city has a Patriot
Day ceremony and it’s great that Mission Viejo does. He also discussed his attendance at the

City Council Minutes  9  September 15, 2014
 Mission for the Armed Forces football game at Mission Viejo High School and a photography
contest event which he attended with Mayor Kelley at the library yesterday.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley agreed that the Patriot Day ceremony on September 11 was very nice and it gave
the residents an opportunity to show gratitude and appreciation for first responders who never
know, when they go to work each day, if they are going to come home. She stated that they are
dedicated and committed to ensuring our safety and she thanked the police officers, firefighters
and members of the armed forces who protect the American way of life and freedom. Mayor
Kelley outlined her attendance at the Mission Viejo High School military support football game
and she stated that it was heartwarming to see 99 veterans being honored on the field with their
corresponding football players. It was also very meaningful to the players to be able to show their
respect for the men and women who have given so much in service to the nation. She reminded
residents that Vietnam veterans will be recognized on September 20 from 11:00 to 3:00 at the
community center and the City is asking for an RSVP for the event. Mayor Kelley discussed her
attendance at a photo contest award ceremony held at the library where she was pleased to present
the participants with recognition certificates. She encouraged residents to visit the library to see
the photographs which will be on display until October 6, 2014. Mayor Kelley reminded residents
of the Inner Coastal Cleanup day project on September 20 at the Oso Creek Trailhead on
Marguerite Parkway from 8:00 a.m. to noon. Participants can register online or at the site. She
also announced that the City of Mission Viejo has been sponsoring American Red Cross blood
drives for the last few years, with approximately 5 blood drives a year. She stated that it makes a
big difference in the community and she thanked the volunteers who work at the blood drives and
AYSO Region 84 which partners with the City. Mayor Kelley noted that President Dave Selecky
stepped up to help and AYSO’s partnership has increased the number of donors. At the last blood
drive, 27 units of blood were collected and in 2014, the City and AYSO Region 84 have helped to
collect a total of 120 units which will help to save up to 360 lives. Mayor Kelley stated that she
was pleased to donate her blood and it made her think about who she could be helping and to be
grateful for her own good health. Mayor Kelley announced that the Community of Character word
for the month of September is responsibility and she read a quote from Booker T. Washington:
“Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him and to let him know
that you trust him.” This month’s free character movie is Frozen which will be shown on Sunday,
September 21 at 2:00 p.m. and Mayor Kelley encouraged residents to attend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:34 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 6, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.
